queries.subject: physics
queries.text: if I multiply two measured lengths how many digits should I keep in the answer
queries.note: Chapter 1, significant figures. The book states the rule; the student asks it as a question about their own working.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: is speed the same thing as velocity or is there a difference
queries.note: Chapter 2. The only chapter-2 concept in the set, so the book's one straight-line-motion chapter is represented.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: if I walk around a park and come back to where I started how much have I moved
queries.note: Displacement does not depend on the path taken. Deliberately phrased with none of the book's own words — no 'displacement', no 'path length' — so the full-text half cannot answer it and only the vector half can.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: does friction depend on how much surface area is touching
queries.note: Written first as 'why is it easier to pull a lawn roller than push it', which the rationalised edition does not cover in the body text; changed to another chapter-4 friction concept that it does.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: why do I get thrown backwards when a bus suddenly starts moving
queries.note: The book uses this exact situation to illustrate the first law, so both halves should find it. Included as a control: a query that fails here indicates something wrong beyond the pin.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: what stops a car from skidding sideways when it takes a turn on a flat road
queries.note: Static friction provides the centripetal force. Key corrected 2026-09-20 after the first scored run, by reading all of §4.10 cold rather than by looking at what ranked. ADDED ¶18 ('On an unbanked road, frictional force alone can provide the centripetal force needed to keep the cyclist moving on a circular turn without slipping'), which answers the question outright and adds the condition under which it fails. REMOVED ¶2, which was keyed in error: it defines centripetal force in general and illustrates it with a stone on a string, and read cold says nothing about a car, a road or skidding. Not added: ¶3, which ranked FIRST in the run and is a section lead-in answering nothing ('The circular motion of a car on a flat and banked road give interesting application of the laws of motion'), and ¶10, a mid-derivation fragment giving v_max.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: if I carry my bag across a flat room have I done any work on it
queries.note: Force perpendicular to displacement does no work. The book's example is a block on a table and the moon's orbit, not a bag, so the wording shares almost nothing with the paragraph.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: a spinning wheel is made of many particles so what is its total kinetic energy 1/2 mv^2 for each one
queries.note: The case the corpus rulings were made for: the book prints its speed glyph as a form of upsilon, and the founder's ruling of 2026-09-17 normalised it to v so that '1/2 mv^2' could reach §6.9 at all. If this query misses, that ruling bought nothing. Key corrected 2026-09-20 after the first scored run, by reading §6.9 cold. ADDED ¶2 ('The total kinetic energy K of the body is then given by the sum of the kinetic energies of individual particles'), which is the question answered in one sentence, and ¶4, which completes it into K = (1/2) I omega^2. REMOVED ¶1, keyed in error: it poses the question ('We have yet to answer one major question') and does not answer it. ¶6 is kept because it is the paragraph carrying the normalised '1/2 m v^2' that the upsilon ruling exists for, though ¶2 and ¶4 are the better answers. Not added: ¶3, a mid-derivation fragment between them.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: किसी वस्तु को घुमाना शुरू करना कितना कठिन होगा यह किन बातों पर निर्भर करता है
queries.note: Hindi → English paragraph. Moment of inertia, asked without naming it in either language — so neither the Hindi tsv half nor a keyword match can carry it and only the cross-lingual vector space can.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: why does a skater spin faster when she pulls her arms in
queries.note: The book's own illustration is a swivel chair, not a skater, so the everyday framing differs from the text while the physics is the same paragraph.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: how fast does a rocket have to go to leave the earth for good
queries.note: Escape speed, 11.2 km/s. Written before the address was looked up; the paragraph that names the number and the one that derives it are both right answers.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: विमीय विश्लेषण से किसी समीकरण के बारे में क्या पता चलता है और क्या नहीं
queries.note: Hindi → English paragraph. What dimensional analysis can and cannot test — the target paragraph is explicitly about its limits.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: जड़त्व किसे कहते हैं और न्यूटन के पहले नियम से इसका क्या संबंध है
queries.note: Hindi → English paragraph, on a concept whose English query (q05) is also in the set — so a Hindi miss beside an English hit isolates the cross-lingual space rather than the corpus.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: बंदूक से गोली चलाने पर बंदूक पीछे क्यों हटती है
queries.note: Hindi → English paragraph. Conservation of momentum, asked as the recoil of a gun, which is the book's own example in that paragraph.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: पृथ्वी की सतह से नीचे जाने पर गुरुत्वीय त्वरण का मान कैसे बदलता है
queries.note: Hindi → English paragraph. g decreases below the surface as well as above it.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: sir photoelectric effect me stopping potential frequency badhane se kyu badhta hai, intensity badhane se kyu nahi badhta
queries.note: Written by the founder in student phrasing and used as written (DECISIONS 2026-10-18). The question is why, so the key is Einstein's explanation in §11.6, read from the rows: ¶2 (intensity is the number of photons, not their energy), ¶4 (K_max linear in frequency, independent of intensity), ¶8 (eV_0 = h nu – phi_0). §11.4.3 states the observations without the reason and is left out.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: पानी से भरी बाल्टी की तली ऊपर उठी हुई क्यों दिखती है असली गहराई से कम
queries.note: Written by the founder in student phrasing and used as written. The book's example is a tank, not a bucket: §9.3 ¶8 says the bottom of a tank filled with water appears raised and gives apparent depth as real depth over the refractive index.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: why does a plastic comb pull small pieces of paper after I run it through my dry hair
queries.note: Claude's draft. Two places answer it: §1.11 ¶9 (the charged comb polarises the uncharged paper, and the field is non-uniform) and Example 2.7's solution, §2.9 ¶17.

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: how does light stay inside an optical fibre all the way to the other end
queries.note: Claude's draft, avoiding the book's term 'total internal reflection'. §9.4.1 ¶2 (the core's refractive index higher than the cladding's) and ¶3 (repeated total internal reflections along the fibre).

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: गरम पानी में रखने पर धातु का कसा हुआ ढक्कन आसानी से क्यों खुल जाता है?
queries.note: Claude's draft; the book's own opening example. §10.5 ¶1 (a tight metal lid put in hot water expands and loosens) and ¶2 (thermal expansion defined).

queries.subject: chemistry
queries.text: SN1 reaction me racemisation kyu hota hai matlab product dono forms me kaise aata hai
queries.note: Written by the founder in student phrasing and used as written. §6.7.1 ¶49: the carbocation of the slow step is planar, the nucleophile attacks from either side, giving both configurations. ¶45 only defines racemisation and is left out.

queries.subject: chemistry
queries.text: if catalyst makes the reaction faster then why doesnt the equilibrium shift or K change
queries.note: Written by the founder in student phrasing and used as written. Two books answer it: chem11-part1 §6.8.5 ¶1 (forward and reverse barriers lowered by the same amount; not in the K expression) and chem12-part1 §3.4.1 ¶5 (K unchanged, equilibrium reached sooner).

queries.subject: chemistry
queries.text: why does water boil at a higher temperature when sugar is dissolved in it
queries.note: Claude's draft. §1.6.2 ¶1 (the solution's vapour pressure must be raised to 1.013 bar, so it boils above 373.15 K; the book's example is sucrose) and ¶2 (elevation of boiling point defined).

queries.subject: chemistry
queries.text: परमाणु के कक्षकों में इलेक्ट्रॉन किस क्रम में भरे जाते हैं?
queries.note: Claude's draft. No Chemistry book has Hindi rows yet (the four move to the beta period), so this reaches English paragraphs through the cross-lingual vector alone. §2.6.4 ¶2 (aufbau: increasing energy) and ¶3 (the order 1s, 2s, 2p …).

queries.subject: chemistry
queries.text: आवर्त में बाएँ से दाएँ जाने पर आयनन एन्थैल्पी क्यों बढ़ती है?
queries.note: Claude's draft; cross-lingual vector alone, as a09. §3.7.1 ¶15: across a period the nuclear charge outweighs the shielding.

queries.subject: biology
queries.text: bhai double fertilisation me ek sperm egg se milta hai to dusra kisse fuse hota hai aur triple fusion ka matlab kya hai
queries.note: Written by the founder in student phrasing and used as written. §1.3 ¶1: the second male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei; three haploid nuclei, hence triple fusion; syngamy plus triple fusion is double fertilisation.

queries.subject: biology
queries.text: why does the second baby get affected when mother is rh negative and father positive but first baby is fine
queries.note: Written by the founder in student phrasing and used as written. bio11 §15.1.3.2 ¶1 carries the whole answer: no exposure in the first pregnancy, exposure at delivery, antibodies in later pregnancies, erythroblastosis foetalis.

queries.subject: biology
queries.text: how can a drop of blood be used to identify a person or find out who the father is
queries.note: Claude's draft, without the term 'DNA fingerprinting'. §5.10 ¶2 (DNA from blood or any tissue identifies a person in forensic use; inherited polymorphisms make it the basis of paternity testing) and ¶5 (a single cell is enough; the forensic application).

queries.subject: biology
queries.text: क्लोरोप्लास्ट में प्रकाश अभिक्रियाएँ कहाँ होती हैं और शर्करा कहाँ बनती है?
queries.note: Claude's draft. §11.3 ¶3: the membrane system traps light and makes ATP and NADPH (light reactions); the stroma's enzymatic reactions make sugar.

queries.subject: biology
queries.text: टीका लगवाने से शरीर बीमारी से कैसे बचता है?
queries.note: Claude's draft. §7.2.4 ¶1: vaccination rests on the immune system's memory; memory B and T cells recognise the pathogen on later exposure.

queries.subject: chemistry
queries.text: what do you get when benzaldehyde is heated with concentrated sodium hydroxide
queries.note: Reaction-pass evidence (DECISIONS 2026-09-29; founder Q3 2026-10-18): an organic reaction the book explains in prose. §8.4 ¶35, Cannizzaro.

queries.subject: chemistry
queries.text: what is formed when ethanal is treated with dilute alkali
queries.note: Reaction-pass evidence. §8.4 ¶31 (aldol reaction) and ¶32 (aldol condensation products).

queries.subject: chemistry
queries.text: how can toluene be turned into benzaldehyde with chromyl chloride
queries.note: Reaction-pass evidence. §8.2.2 ¶7, the Etard reaction.

queries.subject: chemistry
queries.text: what product forms when phenol is treated with chloroform and sodium hydroxide
queries.note: Reaction-pass evidence. §7.4.4 ¶56, the Reimer-Tiemann reaction.

queries.subject: chemistry
queries.text: how is a primary amine made from phthalimide
queries.note: Reaction-pass evidence. §9.4 ¶11, Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.

queries.subject: chemistry
queries.text: acid chloride ko aldehyde mein kaise badalte hain
queries.note: Reaction-pass evidence. §8.2.2 ¶1, Rosenmund reduction.

queries.subject: chemistry
queries.text: रासायनिक साम्य पर दाब बढ़ाने का क्या असर होता है
queries.note: Held out by the founder after the first run, used as written (DECISIONS 2026-10-19). §6.8.2 ¶1 (a pressure change shifts a gaseous equilibrium where the moles of gas differ) and ¶2 (Le Chatelier's principle applied to a compressed mixture). No Chemistry book has Hindi rows.

queries.subject: chemistry
queries.text: carbocation ki stability tertiary > secondary > primary kyu hoti hai
queries.note: Held out by the founder, used as written. The question is why, so the key is the reason: §8.7.1 ¶4 (the order, 'due to inductive and hyperconjugation effects'), §8.7.9 ¶3 (the overlap disperses the positive charge), ¶4 (more alkyl groups, more hyperconjugation), ¶10 (Problem 8.19's worked explanation).

queries.subject: physics
queries.text: प्रत्यावर्ती धारा में संधारित्र वाली धारा वोल्टता से आगे क्यों चलती है
queries.note: Held out by the founder, used as written. The book's only 'why' is the derivation: §7.5 ¶4 (i = dq/dt = omega C v_m cos omega t), ¶5 (cos omega t = sin(omega t + pi/2)), ¶7 (so the current is pi/2 ahead). ¶8 and ¶10 only describe the lead; Claude left them out, applying to h03 the founder's strict reading of 'kyu' for a01 (DECISIONS 2026-10-19), for him to overrule.

queries.subject: biology
queries.text: DNA replication me ek strand continuous aur dusra okazaki fragments me kyu banta hai
queries.note: Held out by the founder, used as written: 'okazaki' is coaching vocabulary the rows never print, kept on purpose so the rewrite must bridge it (founder, 2026-10-19). §5.4.2 ¶2: polymerase works only 5'->3', so replication is continuous on one template and discontinuous on the other, the fragments joined by DNA ligase.
